verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents an official MCP server at https://use.jitsu.com/mcp that lets AI agents create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events and edit Functions. It supports OAuth 2.1 browser approval for interactive clients and personal API keys for headless/CI use, and a probe confirms the dedicated MCP docs page. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of the MCP server working in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Jitsu runs an MCP server, so AI agents can manage your pipeline directly: create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events, and edit Functions.
Point your agent at `https://use.jitsu.com/mcp`, approve it once in the browser, and it can run your data pipeline for you.
For interactive clients, authentication is OAuth 2.1 — you don't paste an API key.
In CI and other headless environments the browser flow can't run. There you authenticate with a personal API key instead
